title: The Advocacy of Christ
sourceBasis: World English Bible — 66-book Old and New Testament Scripture text already installed in Iron Sharpener
definition: The advocacy of Christ is His gracious work as the righteous representative who stands for believers when they sin. Jesus is the Advocate with the Father, and His advocacy rests on His righteousness and atoning sacrifice.
summary: The advocacy of Christ is His gracious work as the righteous representative who stands for believers when they sin. Jesus is the Advocate with the Father, and His advocacy rests on His righteousness and atoning sacrifice.
christFocus: Jesus Christ defends His people not by denying their sin, but by presenting His finished work and righteousness. He is the righteous Advocate who secures mercy for those who belong to Him.

studySections.heading: Doctrine in Summary
studySections.content:
Believers still sin, and Scripture does not invite them to hide or despair. If anyone sins, believers have an Advocate with the Father, Jesus Christ the righteous.

Christ’s advocacy is not permission to sin. John writes so believers may not sin, but also so they know where to turn when they do. The Advocate calls sinners away from hiding and back to grace.

His advocacy rests on His atoning sacrifice. He does not plead that sin is harmless. He stands as the righteous One whose sacrifice answers guilt and whose righteousness belongs to His people.

The accusations of Satan cannot overthrow the work of Christ. The accuser is defeated by the blood of the Lamb, and no charge can stand against those God has justified.

studySections.heading: Why This Matters
studySections.content:
Shame often tells believers to run from God after failure. Religious pride tells them to make excuses. Christ’s advocacy calls them to honest confession and confidence in the righteous Savior.

This doctrine is especially precious for recovering, wounded, and struggling believers. Their hope is not that they never stumble, but that Christ is righteous, sufficient, and faithful.

studySections.heading: Discipleship and Application
studySections.content: When you sin, do not hide, excuse, or collapse in despair. Confess honestly and come to the Father through Christ your Advocate. Then encourage others that restoration is found not in denial, but in the righteous Savior who stands for His people.
